thanks for flagging this and for the screenshot.

We ran into a couple of Calendly/Calendly widget DST/timezone edge cases recently for EU customers where the widget served Pacific times for some browser/cookie combos. Apologies
 that's on us to surface more clearly.

Two quick workarounds that should unblock you immediately:
1) Chili Piper direct scheduling link (alternate): https://www.chilipiper.com/schedule/redwood/demo
 we use this as an alternate; it usually picks up browser timezone more reliably.
2) Manual pick: I can propose three UTC slots and you can pick which maps to morning CEST for you:
   - 2026-07-07 09:00 UTC (11:00 CEST)
   - 2026-07-07 10:30 UTC (12:30 CEST)
   - 2026-07-07 13:00 UTC (15:00 CEST)

If Chili Piper is fine, book there and we'll confirm. If you still see the wrong timezone after trying Chili Piper, reply and I'll create a calendar invite manually (to guarantee correct TZ/ICS).

Cc'ing Alex (platform) and Marissa (CS) so they have context

Subject: Re: Demo scheduling (workaround + notes)

Hi Sofie
 Alex here from Platform. Sorry for the friction. Short version: we have two practical fixes today and a product follow-up ticket.

Workarounds (pick one):
- Force Calendly timezone via URL param: add ?timezone=Europe/Paris to the Calendly scheduling URL. Example: https://calendly.com/redwood/demo?timezone=Europe/Paris
 that forces the widget to show the intended TZ.
- Manual invite: Camila or I can create a Google Calendar invite in Europe/Paris TZ and attach the ICS
 that guarantees correct display across attendees.

Notes on Chili Piper: Chili Piper sometimes omits a separate ICS in the confirmation email depending on the customer flow; their event is still created with a TZ in the backend but we've seen cases where consumer mail clients show the wrong offset if the event's VTIMEZONE block is missing. I attached our local logs from the Chili Piper booking attempt to help debug.

Planned follow-up: I'll file a small product bug to:
1) Surface 'detected timezone' on the scheduling page header for EU users.
2) Add a small fallback that appends timezone param when we detect Europe-based IPs.

Camila
 if you confirm Sofie's preferred slot (11:00 CEST on 2026-07-07), I'll create the manual calendar invite from redwood.ai calendar in Europe/Paris and attach the ICS here.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
